newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka parties appeal for calm in local polls.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka parties appeal for calm in local polls.

text.p: Sri Lanka's two main political parties appealed for calm on Wednesday, the last day of nominations for key local elections next month already marred by the killing of a ruling coalition lawmaker.

Extra police were on duty in election offices around the country as candidates and flag-waving supporters filed applications for the polls, the first electoral test for the ruling People's Alliance since it came to power in 1994.
The elections will be held in seven of the country's nine provinces. The government scrapped polls in the northern and eastern provinces because of guerrilla activity by Tamil separatists.

A total of 3,567 seats in assemblies in 12 cities, 31 towns and 195 villages will be contested, along with mayors for Colombo and 11 other cities. The size of the assemblies ranges from nine seats in remote villages to 53 in Colombo.
Election day is tentatively set for March 27, with a firm date to be announced on Thursday, the Election Department said.

On Tuesday, unknown gunmen killed People's Alliance lawmaker Nalanda Ellawala during a roadside quarrel between his supporters and rivals from the opposition United National Party (UNP), police said. No arrests have been made.

Ellawala's assailants also killed the guard of another ruling party legislator and injured five others in the attack at Kuruwita, 80 km (50 miles) south of Colombo. "I appeal to all sections of the community not to be disturbed by this incident and make every effort to have a peaceful poll," Media Minister Dharmasiri Senanayake said in a statement.
UNP leader Ranil Wickremesinghe urged police to conduct an impartial inquiry into the killing and pave the way for free and fair elections.
"The UNP unequivocally reiterates its position in rejecting this culture of political violence and lawlessness," Wickremesinghe said in a statement.
He said some homes of UNP supporters in Kuruwita were set on fire soon after the shooting which prompted a night curfew in the town. Police said they might re-impose the curfew on Wednesday.

UNP lawmaker Karunasena Kodituwakku said the atmosphere in Colombo was not tense. "We are here with some honourable members of the ruling coalition and the atmosphere is cordial," he told Reuters inside an election office in Colombo.
But others said Tuesday's incident was a sure sign of more election violence to come.

"This is definitely going to spark off a lot of violence between the two major political parties and in the process there will be a lot of violence in the country," Kalinga Indratissa, a lawyer for an independent political group, told Reuters.
Industries Development Minister C.V. Gooneratne said the government would not allow violence to dominate the poll.
"The government will ensure a peaceful election," he said.
